texts.preamble: Munna vs Md. Jawwad on 26 December, 2025
texts.facts: The present Detailed Accident Report (hereafter "DAR") was filed by the investigating officer, ASI Dharambir Singh, in FIR number 811 dated 17.11.2021 lodged at police station Dwarka North under Sections 279/304A of IPC regarding the injuries suffered by the petitioner, Sh. Munna, in a road accident involving a motorcycle bearing registration number DL 9S BW 2429. The DAR was treated as a claim petition under Section 166(4) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter "MV Act"). Respondent no. 1, Md. Jawwad, is the driver, respondent no. 2, Md. Ashrufullah, is the owner and respondent no. 3, Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Company Limited, is the insurer of the said motorcycle. DAR 2. As per the DAR, the petitioner is a resident of Hari Vihar, Kakrola, Delhi. On 16.11.2021, at about 9:45 pm, petitioner, along with his wife, Smt. Sushila, and his daughter, Ms. Sanvi, went to Kakrola Market on his Hero Deluxe motorcycle bearing registration no. DL 4SCK 8068 to purchase shoes. After shopping, while returning towards their house and when the petitioner had started taking a turn towards the same, the offending motorcycle, that is, a Honda Shine bearing registration no. DL 9SBW 2429, on which two persons were riding, came from the side of Kakrola Mor at high speed, being driven in a rash and negligent manner, and struck the petitioner's motorcycle from the right side. As a result of the impact, petitioner, his wife and his daughter fell on the left side of the road and sustained injuries. Petitioner suffered a fracture in his right leg and Ms. Sanvi sustained injuries on her forehead. Smt. Sushila was taken to Tarak Hospital, Delhi, for treatment, where she was declared brought dead. Page No. 2 of 27 Defence of the Respondents 3. Notice of the petition was served on the respondents. 3.1 Respondent nos. 1 and 2 filed their joint written statement, wherein they have, inter alia, claimed that no accident was caused by the motorcycle bearing registration no. DL 9SBW 2429. It is contended that respondent no. 1 was holding a valid and effective driving licence and that the said motorcycle was insured with respondent no. 3 at the time of the accident. 3.2 Respondent no. 3 has admitted that the offending motorcycle was insured with it and filed a legal offer of 88,862/-, after deducting 50% on account of contributory negligence. Thereafter, the claim petition was fixed for petitioner's evidence. Munna vs Md. Jawwad on 26 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18471546/ 2 5. In order to prove his claim, the petitioner examined himself as PW1 and tendered his evidence by way of affidavit and the same is exhibited as Ex. PW1/A. 5.1 The petitioner deposed regarding the manner of the accident consistent with the claims made in the DAR. 5.2 The petitioner has relied on the following documents in support of his MACT No. 912022 Munna vs. Md. Jawwad & Ors. Page No. 3 of 27 testimony: Ex. PW 1/ 2 is his discharge card. Ex. PW 1/3 is the set of his treatment record. Ex. PW1/4 is the set of his medical bills. Ex. PW1/5 is the copy of his Aadhaar card. Ex. PW1/6 is the copy of his PAN card. Ex. PW 1/7 is the DAR. Ex. PW1/8 is his disability certificate no. F.1(1)/DDU/MB/2023/30101 dated 29.09.2023. The disability of the petitioner was assessed by the duly constituted Ortho Board of DDU Hospital in compliance of order of my learned predecessor. 5.3 In his cross-examination, petitioner stated that the offending vehicle had hit his vehicle from the front. He admitted that the road on which the accident occurred was a very busy road. In his further cross-examination, petitioner was confronted with a portion of his statement recorded under Section 161 CrPC by the police (Ex. PW1/R3A), wherein it is stated that he could identify the two boys who were riding the motorcycle which had hit his motorcycle from behind. He volunteered that the offending motorcycle had hit his motorcycle from the front side. He denied the suggestion that the accident was caused by his losing balance of the motorcycle due to his wife holding their daughter in her lap. 6. After completion of petitioner's evidence, the matter was fixed for respondents' evidence. The respondents did not examine any witness. Page No. 4 of 27 Issue No. 1: Whether petitioner sustained injuries in a motor vehicle accident dated 16.11.2021 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle bearing registration no. DL 9SBW 2429 being driven by respondent no. 1 and owned by respondent no. 2? OPP. 8. Onus to prove this issue was on the petitioner. One of these DARs, bearing MACT No. 93/22 titled Munna v. Md. Jawwad, seeking compensation on behalf of Ms. Sanvi, was amicably settled between Sh. Munna and respondent no. 3, Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Company Ltd., for a total sum of 18,000/-. The issue of negligence on the part of respondent no. 1 is to be examined in the light of the evidence brought on record. 17.1 The accident took place on 16.11.2021 at about 9.45 pm and the FIR was lodged by the petitioner on 17.11.2021. Therefore, there was no delay in lodging of the FIR. On completion of investigation, the police filed the charge-sheet against the respondent no. 1 under Sections 279 , 337, 338 and 304A of the IPC showing the involvement of offending motorcycle bearing registration no. DL 9S BW 2429. 17.3 In the criminal case arising out of the accident, the learned JMFC-06, South- West District, Dwarka Court, vide order dated 26.11.2024 passed in Cr. Case no. 2534/2024 titled as State vs. Md. Jawwd has framed charges against the respondent no. 1 for the offences punishable under Sections MACT No. 912022 Munna vs. Md. Jawwad & Ors. Page No. 7 of 27 279/337/338/304A of IPC. 17.4 The arrest memo of the respondent no. 1 shows that he was arrested in the criminal case related to the accident on 28.12.2021. 17.5 Respondent no. 2, in his reply to the notice dated 27.12.2021 issued to him under Section 133 of the Motor Vehicles Act, admitted that respondent no. 1 was driving the offending motorcycle bearing registration no. DL 9SBW 2429 on the day of the accident. He further admitted that his son, Md. Matiullah, was riding as a pillion rider on the said offending motorcycle. 17.6 The Mechanical Inspection Reports dated 20.11.2021 of the motorcycle bearing registration no. DL 4SCK 8068 of the petitioner and the offending motorcycle bearing registration no. DL 9SBW 2429 show that both these motorcycles suffered damage. 17.7As per the seizure memo dated 17.11.2021, the offending motorcycle bearing registration no. DL 9SBW 2429 was seized by ASI Ved Prakash from near the spot of the accident in an accidental condition, with its headlight found broken and its handle bent. The MLIR no. 1513 of the said Tarak Hospital, records that the petitioner was brought to the said hospital with history of road accident and had suffered injury in his right leg. Respondent nos. 1 & 2, being the principal tortfeasors, are primarily liable to make payment of compensation awarded to the petitioner. However, since the offending vehicle bearing registration no. DL 9S BW 2429 was insured by respondent no. 3 against third party risks, therefore, the respondent no. 3 is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
texts.arguments: The petitioner has relied on his testimony as well as the DAR. 9. Learned counsel for respondent nos. 1 & 2 has opposed the petition on the ground that no accident was caused by their motorcycle. 10. Learned counsel for respondent no. 3 has opposed the petition on the ground of contributory negligence on the part of petitioner, as he was triple riding on his motorcycle. 12. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Bimla Devi and Others vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and Others (2009) 13 SCC 530 has held: "15.In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter. 13. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Mangla Ram vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited and Others (2018) 5 Supreme Court Cases 656 has laid down in paragraphs 27 & 28: MACT No. 912022 Munna vs. Md. Jawwad & Ors. Page No. 5 of 27 "27. ... This Court in a recent decision in Dulcina Fernandes, noted that the key of negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle as set up by the claimants was required to be decided by the Tribunal on the touchstone of preponderance of probability and certainly not by standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt. Similarly, even the dictum in Surender Kumar Arora will be of no avail. In the present case, considering the entirety of the pleadings, evidence and circumstances on record and in particular the finding recorded by the Tribunal on the factum of negligence of Respondent 2, the driver of the offending jeep, the High Court committed manifest error in taking a contrary view which, in Munna vs Md. Jawwad on 26 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18471546/ 4 our opinion, is an error apparent on the face of record and manifestly wrong." 14. The Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Smt. Pushpa Rana & Others 2008 (101) DRJ 645 has held: "12. The last contention of the appellant insurance company is that the respondents claimants should have proved negligence on the part of the driver and in this regard the counsel has placed reliance on the judgement of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Meena Variyal; 2007 (5) SCALE 269. On perusal of the award of the Tribunal, it becomes clear that the wife of the deceased had produced (i) certified copy of the criminal record of criminal case in FIR No. 955/2004, pertaining to involvement of the offending vehicle, (ii) criminal record showing completion of investigation of police and issue of charge sheet under Section 279/304-A,IPC against the driver; (iii) certified copy of FIR, wherein criminal case against the driver was lodged; and (iv) recovery memo and mechanical inspection report of offending vehicle and vehicle of the deceased. These documents are sufficient proofs to reach the conclusion that the driver was negligent. Hence, this contention of the counsel for the appellant also falls face down. There is ample evidence on record to prove negligence on the part of the driver." 15. The fact that the motor cycle was hit by the car from behind, is admitted. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 SCC 343 has laid down the general principles relating to compensation in injury cases and held: "6. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalisation, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. Non-pecuniary damages (General damages) (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii) (a) and (iv). It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii)(b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life." The petitioner, in his evidence by way of affidavit, has further claimed that he spent 25,000/- on conveyance and 35,000/- on special diet. However, the petitioner has not produced any bills regarding the same. Keeping in view that the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries resulting in permanent physical disability, the petitioner must have incurred expenses on conveyance and special diet. Therefore, the petitioner is awarded 20,000/- towards special diet and 20,000/- towards conveyance. 30. The petitioner, in his evidence by way of affidavit, has further claimed that he spent 30,000/- on attendant charges. However, no documentary proof regarding hiring of any attendant has been placed on record. 30.1 The Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. Vs. Kumari Lalita 1982 SCC Online Delhi 123 has held that the victim MACT No. 912022 Munna vs. Md. Jawwad & Ors. Page No . 15 of 27 cannot be deprived of compensation towards gratuitous service rendered by some family members for the benefit of tortfeasor. Keeping in view the nature of Munna vs Md. Jawwad on 26 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18471546/ 11 injury of the petitioner and the long period of treatment, a sum of 20,000/- is granted to the petitioner towards attendant charges. Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured Loss of earning during the period of treatment 31. The petitioner, in his evidence by way of affidavit, has further claimed that at the time of accident he was doing a private job in Vipin Garden and earning a sum of 18,000/- to 20,000/- per month. Since the petitioner, being a resident of Delhi, has failed to prove his income, the same is required to be assessed in accordance with the Minimum Wages Act, 1948, as applicable in Delhi. As per the said Act, the minimum wages payable in Delhi to an unskilled worker on 16.11.2021 (the date of the accident) were 16,064/- per month. Accordingly, the said amount is taken as the income of the petitioner (A). 31.3Keeping in view that the petitioner suffered grievous injuries, it is presumed that he would have taken approximately four months to recover from the same. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled to a sum of 16,064/- 4 = 64,256/- towards loss of earning during the period of treatment. As per the law laid down by the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others (2017) 16 SCC 680, the multiplier has to be taken on the basis of the age of MACT No. 912022 Munna vs. Md. Jawwad & Ors. Page No. 16 of 27 the petitioner and for the age group 41-45 years, a multiplier of 14 is applicable. The petitioner is also entitled to addition of 25% of the established income towards future prospects since he was between 40 to 50 years of age at the time of accident. Loss of future earnings is calculated as follows: Annual Income before the accident = 16,064/- x 12 = 1,92,768/- Future Prospects (addition of 25% of the established income)=48,192/- Annual Income including Future Prospects (A)= 2,40,960/- Loss of Future Earning per annum (9 % of A)= 21,686.4 Multiplier applicable with reference to age = 14 Loss of Future Earnings = 21,686.4 x14 = 3,03,609.6 The Hon'ble Supreme Court vide its order dated 16.07.2024 in Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Private Ltd. vs. Union Of India & Ors.
